Robot Doctor Servos

Servo doesn't move

Limp, silent, or does nothing when commanded. Below are the 6 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Is the servo plug the right way around (black/brown wire on ground) at the hub and at every extension? Check the hub label and every joint along the wire.
  • Does the servo resist when you gently try to turn it while the OpMode runs? A powered position servo holds firmly. A limp one turns easily.
  • Does the error say "Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..."? The red error text at the bottom of the Driver Station.
  • Is it supposed to spin continuously (like an intake roller)? Continuous servos spin; position servos go to an angle.
  • Does a known-good servo work in the same spot? Swap in a spare servo without changing anything else.
  • Are several busy servos sharing neighboring ports (0–1, 2–3, 4–5) on the same hub? Count which ports your strong or heavily loaded servos use.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Servo plugged in upside down

Servo plugs fit both ways. Rotated 180°, the servo just sits there.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Match the colors: black (or brown) wire goes to ground. The hub labels the pins.
  2. Check every extension joint too. Each one is another chance to flip it.
  3. Add retaining clips or tape on extensions so they cannot pull apart.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips

2 Servo never gets a position

Hub servo power stays off until the code sends a servo command, so a servo that is never commanded stays limp.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Call setPosition at least once (for example in init) so the port powers up.
  2. Make sure the name in hardwareMap.get matches the configuration exactly.

Sources: GM0 · How the SDK drives servos

3 Servo configured as the wrong type or mode

A continuous servo set up as a regular Servo (or the reverse) does not behave, and some servos have their own modes.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. In the configuration, pick "Servo" for position servos and "Continuous Rotation Servo" for spinning ones.
  2. goBILDA dual-mode and Axon servos can be switched between position and continuous with their programmer. Make sure the servo is in the mode your code expects.
  3. Continuous servos use setPower (CRServo). Position servos use setPosition between 0 and 1.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips · GM0 · How the SDK drives servos

4 Name in code doesn't match the configuration

"Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..." means the string in hardwareMap.get is not exactly the name in the active configuration.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Open the configuration on the Driver Station and compare names letter by letter. They are case sensitive ("leftDrive" is not "LeftDrive").
  2. Make sure the configuration you edited is the active one (its name shows on the DS main screen) and that you saved it.
  3. Watch for trailing spaces in config names.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

5 Servo gears are stripped or the servo is worn

Backdriving a powered servo or side-loading its shaft strips the internal gears.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Swap in a known-good servo. If the problem moves with the servo, the servo is the problem.
  2. Do not force a powered servo by hand.
  3. Support the output with a ServoBlock or bearing, and drive mechanisms through a linkage instead of hanging them right on the spline.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips

6 Servo ports are overloaded

Hub servo ports share power in pairs (0–1, 2–3, 4–5) at about 2 A per pair and 5 A total. Strong servos under load brown out their neighbors.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Spread servos out: FIRST recommends using only the odd or only the even ports, so each servo gets its own pair (up to 3 per hub).
  2. Put heavily loaded servos on a REV Servo Hub or a goBILDA Servo Power Injector (6 V, much more current).
  3. Avoid the old REV Servo Power Module. GM0 warns it can fail and take the hub with it.

Sources: FTC Docs · Servo power best practices · GM0 · Servo usage tips
